study type: Pre/post intervention study with retrospective cohort analysis
exposure: IFH simulation session based on recent guidelines
outcome: Trainee comfort with push, pull, Patwardhan techniques
Faculty comfort with push, pull, Patwardhan techniques
cohort: Thirty-four clinicians (21 trainees, 13 faculty) participated in the simulation session, and clinical impact was assessed using a 6-month pre/post cohort of all patients who underwent second-stage cesarean delivery.
finding: An IFH simulation session improved trainee knowledge and faculty and trainee comfort with the Patwardhan technique, and was associated with a reduction in neonatal intensive care unit admissions.
mod_finding: The simulation session improved obstetrician comfort and knowledge with techniques used during cesarean delivery for impacted fetal head, and was associated with reduced neonatal intensive care unit admissions in patients undergoing second-stage cesarean delivery.
